messages:
rachel: Proposal: unify paged HTTP and a gRPC stream under one iterator API. Prefer stream for low-latency but keep pages as fallback.

tim: 👍 goal is fewer round trips for large result sets, plus nicer async UX in TS/Py.

suzanne: resume is the hard part. server must emit opaque resume tokens periodically. otherwise we risk duplicates/loss on reconnect.

rachel: agree. server header idea: x-resume-token every N items; x-progress-count optional. tokens opaque and versioned.

pete: Go should expose both explicit Stream() and Pages() signatures. hide-nothing for contexts/cancellation.

tim: SDK defaults: prefer_stream=false initially. config: {prefer_stream:true|false, checkpoint_interval:100, stream_retries:3, buffer:64}.

suzanne: retry policy: exponential backoff, try reconnect up to 3 times then fall back to pages using last token. handle auth refresh transparently if possible.

rachel: backpressure: bounded client buffer and optional batch callback to avoid unbounded memory growth.

pete: tests: mid-stream disconnects, auth rotation, memory under slow consumer, billing parity.

ci-bot: CI note: add e2e for fallback + microbench for latency/memory.

suzanne: ops: emit stream lifecycle events so billing/capacity can correlate.

rachel: next step — I'll write follow-up RFC with API sketches for Py/TS/Go and a rollout plan (5% internal canary).

pete: sgtm. small nits: expose stream.meta() with last_resume_token and items_read.

all: ack.
